subject: Telemetry & entitlements: metrics access and SLO measurement details
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: support+procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Telemetry & entitlements: metrics access and SLO measurement details

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Procurement sent over a short questionnaire attached — they want clearer answers about how Redwood measures uptime and latency for the hosted inference endpoints, what alerting looks like, and what access Acme will get to raw telemetry and dashboards. A few specific asks: 

- Exact definitions: how do you compute "availability" and "median latency" for SLOs (time windows, units, which endpoints included)?
- Sampling/aggregation: are metrics aggregated at 1m/5m windows? What sampling rate for high-volume customers?
- Alerting: what thresholds trigger customer-visible alerts vs internal ops alerts? Do customers receive page notifications?
- Data retention & exports: how long are raw per-request logs retained, and can Acme export or stream them to our Splunk/Prometheus?
- Dashboard entitlement: can we create read-only dashboards for our security team or provide API keys for query access?
- Exception paths: if Acme needs a temporary SLO relaxation for a marketing spike (24–72h), what is the process?

I've attached the procurement questionnaire (SLO_Questionnaire_ACME_v1.xlsx). Can your team fill the answers and point to any docs or sample queries we can hand over to our SREs?

Also: we're finalizing contract timelines — if you can indicate typical turnaround for adding a dashboard viewer and granting metric exports, that helps procurement.

Cheers,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Platform Reliability
Acme Corp

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 18:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Telemetry & entitlements: metrics access and SLO measurement details

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list and for sending the questionnaire. We've started filling in the spreadsheet and wanted to provide an interim reply while our docs and a short PromQL sample pack are prepared (Icc'ed Marcus and Rishi for the metric-export and retention answers).

Short answers up front:
- Availability ("uptime") definition: percent of successful inference requests over successful+failed requests, measured per-service per-region, using a rolling 30d window by default. Failure = 5xx responses or internal timeout before token emission.
- Latency SLOs: we report p50/p95/p99 for request-to-first-byte and request-to-last-byte. Aggregation default is 1m buckets; customer-facing SLO calculations use 5m window rollups for stability.
- Sampling & high volume: for extremely high QPS customers we apply consistent hash-based sampling to retain representative per-token timing; default retention for detailed per-request logs is 7 days, aggregated metrics retained 365 days.
- Alerting: internal severity thresholds are configurable. Customers receive email/Slack alerts for Sev-1 incidents (availability < configured SLO threshold for 5 consecutive 5m buckets). We can also provision PagerDuty integration for enterprise plans.
- Exports & dashboards: we support streaming metrics to customer-owned cloud storage (S3/GCS) and a Prometheus remote_write-compatible endpoint for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted plans we provide a read-only Grafana view and API keys scoped to metrics-read.
- Exceptions: temporary SLO relaxations are handled via an Exception Request: we typically require a 72h notice for planned marketing spikes, include a mutual action plan, and log the exception. Unplanned events follow the incident and exception-review workflow; credits are considered per contract.

Attachments: we'll upload a short file with PromQL samples and a link to a shared Grafana view. I'll mark the questionnaire with inline notes and return the spreadsheet by COB tomorrow. If helpful, Marcus can schedule a 30-minute session with your SREs next week to walk through the dashboard and remote_write config.

Best,
Irene 
Irene Choi

Irene, this is perfect — thanks. A couple of clarifications/probes from our SREs and procurement: 

- Can you provide the exact PromQL queries for p95/request-to-last-byte and for the availability calculation (so we can validate against our tooling)?
- For the Prometheus remote_write option: do you have examples for authentication and throughput limits? Is remote_write available to hosted customers or only Dedicated/Private?

If you can attach the sample queries and confirm the retention extension options we can close the questionnaire and move to signing. Also copying our procurement alias to keep the timeline.

Thanks — Liam

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, support+procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Telemetry & entitlements: metrics access and SLO measurement details

Hi Liam — attached are the PromQL samples (promql-samples.txt) and a short note on remote_write auth. Highlights: 

- PromQL samples (copy/paste):
  - Availability (per-region):
    sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total{region="us-east-1",status!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total{region="us-east-1"}[5m]))
  - p95 latency (request-to-last-byte):
    histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

- remote_write: hosted customers can opt-in to streaming metrics to their remote_write endpoint. Authentication is token-based (HMAC token provisioned from Console) and we support per-tenant throttles; sample config included in the attachment. Dedicated/Private allow higher throughput and continuous bleed of raw logs to S3/GCS for up to 90/365 days by contract.
- Retention extension: yes — we can offer per-request log streaming to customer S3 for 90 days as a paid add-on. We'll include estimated egress and storage cost in the commercial brief.
- Exception approvals: for planned marketing spikes (24–72h) email approvals are acceptable for operational SLO relaxations; for changes that modify contractual SLAs (credits, permanent SLO change) we require a signed amendment.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We finish the questionnaire answers and upload the completed XLSX to your procurement link by EOD tomorrow.
2) Marcus will set up a 30-minute Grafana walkthrough and remote_write example session with your SREs (I'll propose times).
3) Commercial will scope the 90-day raw-log export add-on and include pricing and egress estimate.

If that plan looks good, we'll mark the thread as "ready for signature" once procurement confirms.

Best,
Irene
